title: Cambodia Protests Thai House Demolitions, Bunker and Well Construction in Contested Sectors
detail: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement listing a sequence of Thai military activities on land it claims as its own: on August 31, Thai forces demolished two civilian houses in the Boeung Trakuon area of Trapeang Samraong village, Thmar Puok district, Banteay Meanchey province, then leveled the ground and raised an earthen embankment; from September 1-3, heavy machinery was used to build military bunkers near O'Khla Khmum Pagoda in O'Smach, Oddar Meanchey province; from September 4-7 a well was drilled at Chouk Chey village, O'Chrov district; and on September 7 further civilian structures were demolished at nearby Prey Chan village. The statement followed Cambodia's separate protest over the September 7 ASEAN Observer Team visit to Thai-held buildings near the Royal O'Smach Hotel.

media.caption: Cambodia protests Thai house demolitions, bunker construction and well drilling in contested border sectors

title: Information Minister: 'A Ceasefire Is Not a Title Deed to Territory'
detail: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra argued that the December 27, 2025 ceasefire freezes military positions but confers no territorial rights, saying 'freezing troop positions is not the same as freezing sovereignty. Troop positions are not international boundaries. Factual control is not legal title.' He said Thailand cannot isolate paragraph 2 of the Joint Statement (maintaining troop positions) from paragraphs 3, 4 and 6, which bar creating new facts on the ground or obstructing civilian returns, noting roughly 20,000 displaced Cambodian civilians still cannot go home. Any barbed wire, trenches, fortifications or roads built since the ceasefire, he said, amount to unlawful consolidation rather than mere position maintenance: 'A ceasefire is not a title deed to territory.'

media.caption: Cambodia's Information Minister says the ceasefire does not confer territorial rights over Thai-held land
